title: Stripping Mutability Context in Type-Erased API Boundaries
pattern: Returning a generic, flat type-erased container from an interface, discarding the mutability invariants of the underlying fields.
why_bad: It prevents the type system from enforcing write safety. Callers can mistakenly attempt to edit fields that are read-only, causing runtime exceptions.
detection: Traits returning generic flat collections like maps or lists that strip variance and mutability tags of individual fields.
fix:
Use distinct type wrappers or explicit fields to preserve mutability constraints.
```rust
struct Field {
    value: String,
    is_writable: bool,
}
```
source: *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 204, Section 14.1 - variance/record mutability).
